title: An agent asks to resize a scratch pane
body:
decade's MCP tools let an agent start a program in a scratch pane (`scratch.open`), capture what it draws (`screenshot`) and record it (`record`). No tool sets the pane's size, so the pane is whatever size the layout gives it. A README recording needs a set size: a GIF about twice as wide in pixels as GitHub shows it, with the terminal inside at a set number of columns and rows. Today the person drags the pane by eye while the agent reads the size back.

## Proposal

- An MCP tool `scratch.resize` takes a scratch pane's name and a width and height in pixels.
- decade asks the person every time. Unlike `screenshot` and `record`, no pane mode lets a resize through without asking.
- The answer gives the size the pane ended up with, which can differ from the request when the layout cannot fit it.

## Open

- How the layout makes room: by shrinking the neighbouring panes, by floating the pane, or by refusing a size that does not fit.
- Whether the pane goes back to its old size when its program exits, or only when an agent asks.
